correctness.rationale: For invertible quotient adjacency, the neighbor-sum vectors w_i are independent, so rank L_x equals the number of nonzero clone blocks. An isomorphism permutes these maximal rank-one spaces; square identities give conformal orthogonal block maps and a size-preserving quotient automorphism. Edge equations c_i^2=c_j d_j and connectivity force regularity on a nonbipartite quotient or biregularity on its bipartition. Explicit positive diagonal scalings give the converse. Real positivity, no isolated vertices, and nonsingular H are essential; clone expansions may have singular adjacency.
